lessons.label: Reading 1
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Present simple to describe personality (e.g. I’m kind Sara.) and expectations (e.g. This year I want to…)

pre: Play vocabulary game to activate knowledge of words learned in previous years. Focus on word sets pupils will use in this lesson (personality adjectives, family, school subjects, free- time activities and holidays). Choose an activity from the pre-lesson task list in Section 3 of this document.
delivery: Introduce yourself and describe your personality with an adjective, e.g. Hi! I’m kind Sara. Have pupils brainstorm personality adjectives and introduce themselves in groups. Ask pupils to make name cards (this could be done at home) showing their personality and their name.

Ask the pre-reading question in the Teacher’s Book for Warm-up: The big picture (Where are they?). Then ask pupils to read the short texts in the Pupil’s Book, p.4. Ask pupils which of the children they agree with most and what they would like to learn about this year.

Ask for two or three volunteers to introduce themselves to the class using the texts as a model. Ask all pupils to introduce themselves to their partner, using the texts and the volunteers as a model. Monitor as pupils do this to get an impression of individuals’ levels in your class.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.18, for Activity 1. Pupils listen to the four children talking about themselves. Have them read the audio script as they listen.
Pupils read the script again. Ask a question to check their overall understanding of the text, for example: Which child are you similar to? Pupils tell their partner.
Ask pupils to note two things about themselves in their notebooks.
Using these notes and the personality adjective, ask pupils to write at least two sentences about themselves.
post: Pupils introduce themselves in new groups by reading their self-introduction.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 4–5 Exercise(s): 1 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 18 Copy the audio script for each pupil
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider asking some pupils to explain more about their personality, their expectations for the year and what they hope to contribute to the class (CCE: Values).

lessons.label: Writing 1
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Present simple questions & answers to talk about oneself (e.g. How many people are there in your family?)

pre: Review previous lesson’s personality adjectives and pupils’ names with a short class quiz: ‘Who is [kind]?’ Ask pupils to display their name cards.
delivery: Briefly review the content of Activity 1 (Pupil’s Book, p.5) by asking pupils what they remember about the four children. They can check what they remember by looking at their answers to Activity 1 from the previous lesson.

Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book (p.19) for Activity 2. Pupils work individually to write questions. Support your pupils as necessary by writing gapped questions on the board when eliciting these before the pupils write. If pupils find this challenging, review present simple questions at this stage.
Pupils use their questions to ask a partner about themselves. They should check the accuracy of their questions as they do this. Monitor to assess pupils’ ability to write questions.
Based on the instructions for Activity 3 (Teacher’s Book, p.19), pupils should ask members of their group (4–6 pupils) the questions and make a note of the answers.
Ask pupils to write about their group in their notebooks.
Pupils share their writing with their group and ask each other to check content and language.
post: Choose a post-lesson task from Section 3 to review content and/or language pupils had difficulty with during the lesson.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 5 Exercise(s): 2–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 19
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider grouping less with more proficient pupils, so they can help support each other. In Step 6, set a minimum number of pupils to write about, e.g. Write about at least two members of your group.

lessons.label: Listening 1
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Present simple for defining vocabulary (e.g. This is a person who…)

pre: Play a game to introduce the two topics (jobs & places), for example Beat the Teacher (see Pre-lesson Task 7).
delivery: Follow the instructions for Warm-up in the Teacher’s Book, p.20 – pupils listen to words and categorise them.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 (Teacher’s Book, p.20) – pupils find words in the picture.

Review answers to Step 3 by having pupils listen to the word and point to the picture. Drill the new words as they point. Focus on difficult sounds and word stress of longer words such as photographer, businesswoman and police officer. Ask pupils to count the syllables with their fingers and highlight the stressed syllable as they say the longer words.

Read aloud the definitions you have prepared. Pupils listen to your definitions and try to find the words you are describing. They should write the words. [E.g. This is a person who rides the waves on a board].
Check answers and draw attention to spelling where needed.
Have pupils prepare some similar definitions and play the game in small groups.
post: Review learning by asking pupils to say which words they often use in their own daily lives.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 6–7 Exercise(s): 1 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 20 Prepare 4 or 5 definitions for vocabulary items
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider pre- writing some definitions for less proficient pupils to choose from in Step 7.

lessons.label: Speaking 1
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Present simple for descriptions (e.g. A chef is coming out of the shop.)

pre: Review new or difficult vocabulary from the previous lesson using an activity from the
task list in Section 3.
delivery: Follow instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.21, for the Cooler true-false activity.

Follow instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.20, for Activity 2. Tell pupils to focus on spelling in this activity. As you monitor and when you conduct feedback, note words which pupils spelled incorrectly. These can be used at the post-lesson stage.
Follow instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.20, for Activity 3, but pupils first say two true and two false statements in pairs. Then together, they write their statements in their notebooks.

Pairs join another pair. Pupils read the other pair’s statements and decide which are true and which are false. They explain their answer to the other pair. Monitor and check pupils’ work as they do this activity. Note examples of common mistakes for Step 6.
post: On the board, write one or two sentences pupils made mistakes in. Ask pupils to work with a partner to say the correct sentence.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 6–7 Exercise(s): 2–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 20–21
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider asking fast finishers to write more sentences about the picture or about the classroom. They could read these to the class at the end of Step 6.

lessons.label: Language Arts 1
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family, and Friends
lessons.focus: Reported speech (e.g. He said he sat in some glue.)

pre: Pupils look at the pictures around the poem and talk about them.
Pupils guess what the poem is about.
delivery: Recite the poem and pupils repeat after.
Pupils do the gestures as they recite the poem e.g. jumping, kicking, thirsty, sticky
Elicit from the pupils on who they can relate to best: Jumping John, Kicking Kirsty, Mad Mickey or Fat Fred.
Demonstrate how to perform a jazz chant for the first stanza.
Help pupils to identify the stress and rhythm by clapping hands or snapping fingers in time to the beat.
In groups, pupils recite the poem in a form of a jazz chant.
post: Pupils assess each group’s recitation using Two Stars and a Wish: two things that are good (stars) and one thing that can be improved (wish).

lessons.materials: Anthology of Poems for Year 4,5, and 6 Messing About by Michael Rosen Page: 27 Contemporary Children’s Literature Teaching Guidebook (BPK) – Poetry
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils and class. Please see the seven differentiation strategies listed in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider pairing less with more proficient pupils, so they can help support each other in Step 8.

lessons.label: Reading 2
lessons.focus: Introduction to past simple & past continuous

pre: Write electricity on the board and have pupils brainstorm uses of electricity in small groups. This could be done as a game.
delivery: Elicit different meanings of the word power, including as a synonym for electricity. Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.22, for Activity 1. Pupils discuss the questions.
Talk to the pupils about prediction skills in reading (see ‘Teaching Star’, Teacher’s Book, p.22) and encourage prediction based on the pictures.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.23. Pupils analyse the text to decide on the text type.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.23. Pupils further analyse the text to identify different features of it.
Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.23. Pupils search for words in the text and use context clues to guess meaning.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.24. Pupils look for detail in the text to answer questions.
Ask pupils to re-read the text to find something interesting and tell their partner.
Talk to pupils and lead a discussion about our increasing need for and reliance on electricity and power as we use more and more electronics (CCE: Global sustainability and Science & Technology).
post: 9. Follow instructions for the Cooler memory game activity in the Teacher’s Book, p.23.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 8–10 Exercise(s): 1–4; 1 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 22–24
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider giving step-by-step guidance at Step 6. This may be a new skill for pupils. If some of your pupils may find this difficult, you could give them alternative definitions to choose from or create a word- definition matching activity.

lessons.label: Writing 2
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Past simple & continuous for interrupted actions with when

pre: Briefly review the text from the previous lesson by asking some true/false questions. Then have pupils discuss the questions in Activity 3 (Pupil’s Book, p.10).
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.26. Pupils see and analyse the new language.
Follow the instructions in ‘Personalisation’ in the Teacher’s Book, p.26. Pupils relate the new language to their own lives.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.26. Pupils read and choose the correct words.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.27. Pupils use prompts to make sentences.

Pupils work in pairs. They cut a piece paper into 6, 8 or 10 equal small pieces of paper using a grid. On each small piece of paper, they write a sentence in the past simple. Write an example on the board to show pupils what to do. They can use the examples in Activity 3 for ideas.

In pairs put the small papers together in a pile. In turns, they take two papers from the pile and try to make a sentence using the target language (e.g. I was xxx-ing when xxx.) Pupils write the sentences in their notebooks.
Have some pairs tell the class any funny sentences they made.
post: Choose a post-lesson task from Section 3 to review content and/or language pupils had difficulty with during the lesson.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 10–11 Exercise(s): 3; 1– 3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 26–27 Plain paper for each pupil Scissors
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. At Steps 3 and 6, differentiate by the number of sentences/cards pupils create.

lessons.label: Listening 2
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Past simple & continuous for interrupted actions with when/while

pre: Choose an activity from the Pre-Lesson Tasks in Section 3 to review vocabulary from the unit so far.
delivery: Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.30 for Activity 1. Pupils match words and pictures before listening.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, pp.30–31 for Activity 2. Pupils listen for the main idea and check their answers in Activity 1.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.31 for Activity 3. Pupils listen again to answer the questions.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.31 for Activity 4. Pupils answer the questions then listen again for detail to check their answers.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.31 for Activity 5. Pupils discuss the questions to follow up on the listening activity topic.
Elicit the Values from pupils (Pupil’s Book, p.13) and discuss this question with the class (CCE: Values).
post: Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book for the Cooler choose a job activity or choose an activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3 to review content and vocabulary.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 13 Exercise(s): 1–5 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 30–31
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider asking pupils to plan their answers to the discussion questions before discussing in pairs. Think about pairing higher proficiency learners together so that they can benefit from the extra practice. You could ask them a third discussion question.

lessons.label: Speaking 2
lessons.focus: Past simple & continuous for interrupted actions with when/while

pre: Use the clock/clock face to show different times. Ask pupils to tell their partner what they were doing at that time yesterday/on Saturday/etc. Monitor and remind pupils of the use of past continuous if necessary.
delivery: Introduce the pupils to the dictionary in the Pupil’s Book (see Vocabulary instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.28).
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.28. Pupils are introduced to the dialogue.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.28. Pupils read and complete the text with when or while.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, pp.28–29. Pupils match actions and activities.

Pupils work in pairs. They take one or two ideas from Activity 3 or from the unit as a whole, or they use their own ideas to create a story. Pupils make detailed notes about their story in pairs and practise telling their story. Remind pupils to use the target language with when and/or while.
post: Choose some pupils to tell their stories to the class. Have the class decide which story is most exciting/interesting/frightening etc. If you have a large class or time is short, pairs could tell their stories in larger groups.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 12 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 28–29 A toy clock (or draw a clock face on the board before the lesson)
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider setting different limits/targets or minimum word limits/targets for different pairs, for example: Use at least 10 verbs/ Speak for at least 30 seconds.

lessons.label: Language Arts 2
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Adjectives: describing personalities (e.g. cheerful, angelic)

pre: Pupils recap the events from the poem.
delivery: Drill on the alliteration in the poem e.g. Mad Mickey, Fat Fred
Pupils brainstorm adjectives that start with the same letter as their first name e.g. Angelic Adam, Funny Farah, Sleepy Sarah
Pupils take turns to talk about their names and adjectives.
Pupils chant their new names with actions.
post: Each pupil gets a race template. (See Appendix 1)
Pupils fill out the race template with adjectives using the first letter of their names.
In pairs, pupils do peer-assessment and count the stars collected.

lessons.materials: Anthology of Poems for Year 4,5, and 6 Messing About by Michael Rosen Page: 27
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider some pupils may not be able to come out with their own adjectives. You may assist them with examples or gestures to prompt their ideas in Step 3.

lessons.label: Reading 3
lessons.focus: Direct speech, e.g. Lena said, ‘I was playing badminton at 5 o’clock.’

pre: Elicit the topic of the text pupils read at the beginning of the unit. Read the sentences you prepared and ask pupils to vote if they are true or false.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.32. Pupils find and analyse direct speech in the text.
Ask pupils to read the text in detail to find more examples of direct speech in the text. Focus in particular on punctuation as well as use of direct speech.

In pairs, pupils ask each other some questions: What were you doing at 8 o’clock yesterday evening? How did you feel? What else happened to you yesterday? Pupils make notes about their partner’s answers.

Pupils report on one or two answers in their notebooks using direct speech, e.g. Hasan said, ‘I was having dinner at 8 o’clock.’ Ask fast finishers to write more answers. Alternatively, they could help you monitor their peers and check their punctuation.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.32. Pupils read for detail to match the questions to the notes.
post: Finish the lesson with a quiz or reading race based on the text on p.9 of the Pupil’s Book.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 9, 14 Exercise(s): 1–2 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 32 3 or 4 true/false sentences based on what different people say in the text on Pupil’s Book, p.9
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider adding a further practice activity which focuses on punctuation in direct speech if this is new to your pupils.

lessons.label: Writing 3
lessons.focus: Past simple & continuous for interrupted actions with when/while; Direct speech

pre: Play a mime game to review the words in Working with words (Pupil’s Book, p.15).
delivery: Follow the instructions for Working with words in the Teacher’s Book, p.32. Extend this activity with more examples if relevant, such as bored/boring; shocked/shocking.
Give pupils the worksheet. First, ask pupils to highlight the headline and underline any direct speech.
Next, pupils read the jumbled sections of the newspaper article and decide which paragraph(s) are the introduction/main body/conclusion.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.33 for the Workbook Activity 1 (see Activity 1 of Prepare to Write, p.14). Pupils order the pictures to tell a story.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.33 for the Workbook Activities 2 & 3. Pupils organise ideas into the main sections (introduction, main body, conclusion).

Follow instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.33 for the Workbook Activity 4, p.15. Pupils write a newspaper article. Remind pupils to include adjectives, direct speech and interrupted actions. Note that this activity helps pupils develop organisational and narrative skills for the Speaking Assessment, where they should narrate a story based on picture prompts.
post: Have pupils choose an adjective from Step 2 to make a sentence about their newspaper story. Remind pupils to bring their writing to the next lesson.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 15 Exercise(s): 3 & Working with words Workbook: Pages: 14–15 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 32-33 Worksheet: A newspaper article (around 100 words) based on Activity 3 in Pupil’s Book, p.15, in jumbled paragraphs (Introduction, 2 x main body, conclusion), with a headline and including direct speech.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. You could ask pupils to finish this at home if they don’t have time to complete it during the lesson.

lessons.label: Listening 3
lessons.focus: Should(n’t) for giving advice

pre: Review homework by asking pupils to review each other’s writing using the questions in Activity 5 on p.15 of the Workbook.
delivery: Follow instructions in the Teacher’s Book p.36 for the Warm-up activity. Pupils share their ideas for how to ask for help in an emergency.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.36 for Activity 1. Pupils read and analyse a short text to identify parts of a problem.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.36 for Activity 2. Pupils anticipate problems based on pictures to predict what they will hear.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.36 for Activity 3. Pupils listen for detail to see if they were correct in Step 4.

Based on the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.36 for Activity 4, have pupils work in pairs. Set up this activity as a role play, where one pupil plays the part of Mike Dobbs, and the other pupil gives him advice to solve the problem using expressions such as I think you should(n’t)… because… Remind pupils to explain the reasons for the advice they give. The advice should be based on what they hear in the listening activity. Replay this if necessary. (CCE: Values, helping others)
Ask some pupils to perform their role play to the class.
post: Choose a post-lesson task from Section 3 which reviews the content of the listening or language for giving advice, depending on the needs of your class.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 17 Exercise(s): 1–4 Workbook: Page: 15 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 36
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider giving pupils support at Step 6 to help them with ideas. You may also want to model the language by asking a more proficient pair to demonstrate to the class.

lessons.label: Speaking 3
lessons.focus: Reporting verbs (ways of speaking (e.g. whisper) & questions in the past (e.g. how did you feel?)

pre: Choose an activity from the Pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 to review key vocabulary for storytelling and reporting, such as -ed/-ing adjectives.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Vocabulary in the Teacher’s Book, p.34. Pupils work with definitions and use the dictionary at the back of the book. Remind them to use this dictionary when they need to, especially when they are reviewing the lessons at home.
Follow the instructions for Activities 1 & 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.34. Pupils match the sentences to pictures and then listen to check their answers.
Follow the instructions for Activities 3 & 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.34. Pupils listen and decide how the speaker is speaking then practice speaking in different ways.
Follow the instructions for Activity 5 in the Teacher’s Book, p.35. Pupils listen to the reporter’s questions and choose the best answers.
Pupils listen again to the questions. They write the questions they hear next to the answers in the Pupil’s Book (Activity 5, p.16).

Follow the instructions for Activity 6 in the Teacher’s Book, p.35. Pupils act out the emergency in small groups. Have them act as well as they can, showing emotion and using different voices. Encourage creativity in this activity (CCE: Creativity & Innovation).
Depending on time available, have one or more groups perform to the class.
post: Write a quote on the board from the story, using correct punctuation. Ask pupils to say the spoken text in different voices (e.g. whisper, shout, etc.)

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 16 Exercise(s): 1–6 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 34–35
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider assigning a director for Step 7, who helps the group act. They should use English for this but do not need to perform themselves.

lessons.label: Language Arts 3
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Nouns

pre: Give lyrics to pupils to sing along. (Refer to the guidebook)
Pupils listen to a short song about sandwich. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wUDqQSwdBjM
delivery: Pupils recite the poem aloud with guidance .
Pupils call out the ingredients found in the poem.
Each pupil gets The Silly Sandwich template. (Appendix 1)
Pupils write down 10 ingredients they wish to put in their Silly Sandwich.
Pupils draw the ingredients on The Silly Sandwich template.
post: Pupils present and explain their choice of ingredients.

lessons.materials: Anthology of Poems for Year 4,5, and 6 The Sandwich by Tony Bradman Page(s): 28-29 http://www.youtub e.com/watch?v=w UDqQSwdBjM Contemporary Children’s Literature Teaching Guidebook (BPK) – Poetry
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider giving a little more time to finish for some pupils who need longer than others to complete tasks, especially when writing is involved and extra tasks for pupils who complete the task early should be provided.

lessons.label: Language Awareness 1
lessons.focus: Teacher to complete:

std.note: Language Awareness lessons should be presented and practised using a Main Skill and a Complementary Skill (Listening, Speaking, Reading or Writing). Teachers can use the Content and Learning Standards in the Year 6 DSKP.

pre: Review language from Unit 1 with an activity from the list of pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17 for more ideas.
delivery: Choose from activities from the Workbook Check-up challenge, pp.16–17, which reviews the language, vocabulary and skills covered in this unit. This choice should be based on your observations and notes on pupils’ progress and achievement in these units. Choose activities which will review areas pupils found challenging or which they may have forgotten. You could have pupils choose for themselves what they would like to do in this review lesson. See Teacher’s Book, p.37 for instructions and answer keys for activities.

Have pupils do a Speaking task in pairs which is based on the Unit 1 or Welcome Unit theme. Monitor as they do this and note their performance. Note: ● Plan any further activities for this unit to develop language skills according to your pupils’ needs. ● You can use information about your pupils’ performance which you collected using formative assessment strategies while teaching this unit. ● The information could include your observation of pupils interacting in classroom activities and their performance in written activities. ● Plan activities which focus on language practice in a meaningful, fun and communicative way.
post: Ask pupils to think about their learning and performance in this unit. They then complete the self-assessment worksheet. Pupils should do this in English (see below).
Collect the worksheets from pupils and review them to note pupils’ responses. If there are any areas of concern, prepare a review of these in upcoming lessons.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 37 Workbook: Page(s): 16–17 Worksheet: A speaking task. Self-assessment worksheet (see below)
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. Ask pupils to do the self-assessment in English. Monitor and give support to less proficient pupils as needed.

lessons.label: Reading 4
lessons.focus: Used to / didn’t use to

pre: Show the pictures of London in the 17 th century and ask pupils what they can see, where they think it is, which century it is in, etc. Note any useful key vocabulary on the board.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book p.42. Use the picture of Samuel Pepys (pronounced: /piːps/) as you introduce pupils to him.
Follow instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.43. Pupils look at each picture and talk about what they see.
Follow instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.43. Pupils read to check their answers and to gain a global understanding of the text.
Follow instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.43. Support and guide pupils as they develop the skill of guessing meaning from context.

Talk to pupils about how they record new vocabulary. You may have a system set up for this, such as using a special section of their notebooks, having a separate vocabulary notebook or using vocabulary cards (see Teacher’s Book, p.43). Encourage pupils to write definitions of new words in English and avoid translations unless necessary, especially in the case of more proficient pupils.

The Great Fire of London was a tragic event, but it helped eradicate the plague. Ask pupils to reflect on positive and negative outcomes of these events. (CCE: Global Sustainability). Support pupils in expressing their ideas in English by helping them with vocabulary and language if they speak in their home language.
post: Review new vocabulary in the lesson with an activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17, for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 22–23 Exercise(s): 1–4 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 42–43 Pictures / illustrations of 17 th century London, the Great Fire of London and Samuel Pepys, if possible. Pictures / illustrations of any similar well-known events from local or national history
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider playing the recording as pupils read along in Step 4. This will help them to read more fluently as they won’t be able to keep stopping or stumbling over new words.

lessons.label: Writing 4
lessons.focus: Used to / didn’t use to

pre: Use the pictures from Lesson 17 (both those from the UK and from Malaysia) to review vocabulary and historical content through a guessing game or another lively activity.
delivery: Ask pupils to remember the text in the Pupil’s Book pp.22–3 to order the sentences in Activity 1 in the Pupil’s Book, p.24. They should then read quickly to check their answers.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.44. Pupils will need to think carefully to answer the questions.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.45. Pupils discuss the questions comparing life in the past with now. Ask pupils to focus on life in London at this stage.

Ask pupils if the same differences can be found in their hometown or in Kuala Lumpur, as the capital city. Ask pupils in pairs to brainstorm similarities and differences between life in the past (e.g. 50 or 100 years ago) and life now.

Working on a computer, where available, ask pupils to create a table to show the similarities and differences. They could colour their table and find some illustrations to support their ideas. Encourage them to use an online dictionary to check spelling or to find words they don’t know, or they can ask for your help (in English). If you are not using a computer, encourage pupils to use printed dictionaries.
Put two pairs together to read and review each other’s work. They should make changes and corrections as necessary. Monitor carefully at this stage to manage peer feedback.

If you have a class blog or website, have pupils upload their work so they can look at each other’s tables. If you don’t have access to computers, pupils can create posters and display them in the classroom.
post: 8. Conduct a gallery walk for pupils to give each other feedback on their work – pupils move around the classroom, look at each other’s work and comment on it. Collect pupils’ work at the end of the lesson to review it.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 22–24 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 44–45 Pictures from Lesson 17 Computers or posters, stationery and dictionaries
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider setting a target for the number of similarities and differences. Elicit and leave plenty of vocabulary on the board at Step 1 to support pupils in their writing. Monitor actively as pupils write to help with ideas and language.

lessons.label: Listening 4
lessons.focus: Used to / didn’t use to

pre: Play a whole class or large group game using the nouns and verbs from Working With Words (Pupil’s Book, p.24). This could be ‘Listen and touch/run’, ‘Match on the board/large paper’, for example. Include write – writer. Ask pupils if they remember Samuel Pepys’ job (he was a writer).
delivery: Elicit some ideas from pupils about how people lived in London in Pepys’ time. Elicit more ideas about how pupils’ grandparents lived. Note useful ideas on the board.
Follow instructions for Vocabulary in the Teacher’s Book, p.48 to introduce vocabulary.

Follow instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.48. When asking questions to model used to, ask about pupils’ grandparents and/or Samuel Pepys. (CCE: Patriotism, finding out about local heritage).

Play the recording of the dialogue again. Have pupils listen for the pronunciation of used to (/'juːstə/). Point out that the pronunciation is different for use as a verb on its own. Drill several times chorally and individually, having pupils focus on their pronunciation while saying full positive and negative sentences and questions. Have pupils repeat in different voices to review whisper, shout, scream etc.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.48. Pupils use prompts to make a new dialogue.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.48. Pupils form questions using used to.
Drill the questions and check pupils’ pronunciation of used to again before having them practice the questions and answers (Activity 4, Pupil’s Book, p.26).
post: Follow the instructions for the Cooler Tic-tac-toe activity in the Teacher’s Book, p.48 or choose an activity from the post-lesson tasks to review areas of learning in this lesson that pupils have had difficulty with.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 24 & 26 Exercise(s): 1–4 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 48
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider drilling chorally as a whole class and then in pairs or small groups, rather than individually, if you have very shy pupils in your class.

lessons.label: Speaking 4
lessons.focus: Used to / didn’t use to

pre: Using the examples from pupils’ work from Lesson 18, say some sentences in the form they are written (pupils may have used present simple, past simple, or some may have used used to). In small groups, pupils listen and write a full sentence using used to when suitable. Repeat three or four times. Review and check as a whole class.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Warm-up: What can you see? in the Teacher’s Book, p.46, to focus attention on the language in context.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.46 to guide pupils to notice the target language form and meaning.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.46. Pupils complete the text using the target language.
Give pupils back their writing from Lesson 18. Have pupils use their similarities and differences to say sentences using used to/didn’t use to.

Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.46. Pupils talk to their partner about when they were three years old. Extend the activity by asking pupils to give one incorrect piece of information about themselves. Partners should guess which information is incorrect.

Individually, pupils write a short paragraph about their life in the past (e.g. when they were three years old). Set a word limit (see differentiation strategies) and consider having pupils finish for homework. Collect their work to evaluate their writing and language progress; adjust your upcoming teaching plans if you need to review particular areas or work more with individuals.
post: Consolidate learning with a speaking activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 25 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 46-47 Examples of past statements from pupils’ work from Lesson 18.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider setting different targets for different pupils or allowing pupils to write as much (or as little) as they like. This will also give you formative feedback on motivation and attitude.

lessons.label: Language Arts 4
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Adverbs: sequencing, e.g. First… Next… After that, punctuation

pre: See Section 3, Pre-lesson Task 9: Memory Chain. Use the sentence: I want to put tomatoes in my sandwich... I want to put tomatoes and cucumbers in my sandwich. I want to put tomatoes, cucumbers and … in my sandwich
delivery: Distribute a Flow Map to each group. (Appendix 1)
Pupils watch a short clip on how to make a sandwich. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G4BSk1U5ans
In groups, pupils fill in the Flow Map with correct information.
Pupils discuss the steps of making a sandwich.
In groups, pupils prepare their sandwiches.
post: Conduct a gallery walk, where pupils walk around and look at each other’s Flow Maps. Have groups talk about their Flow Maps as you do this, in a casual way, focussing on sequencing adverbs and punctuation.

lessons.materials: Anthology of Poems Year 4,5, and 6 The Sandwich by Tony Bradman Page(s): 28-29 https://www.youtu be.com/watch?v= G4BSk1U5ans Contemporary Children’s Literature Teaching Guidebook (BPK) – Poetry Note to teacher: Remind pupils earlier to bring: - their own favourite ingredients for the sandwich.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider grouping less proficient pupils with more proficient pupils, so they can help support each other.

lessons.label: Reading 5
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Informal written language (e.g. Yuck!; Ha! Ha! Ha!)

pre: Show pupils the picture/extract from a diary and ask pupils what they can see. Ask who they have learned about that kept a diary (Samuel Pepys). Show (or explain) how a blog can be a diary too. Elicit sentences to compare diaries in the past and now using used to. Ask pupils about their own diary-keeping habits.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.52. Pupils analyse Pepys’ diary content.

Ask pupils to read Gemma’s diary (Pupil’s Book, p.28). Ask a gist question such as Do you think Gemma had a good day? Why/Why not? Have pupils exchange their ideas in pairs before whole-class feedback.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.52. Pupils read and consider the style of the example diary entry.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.52. Pupils identify informal language in the diary.

Ask pupils to read the diary entry again. They should underline or highlight anything in the diary that was also true for them yesterday. It is possible that some pupils don’t underline anything. Conduct feedback as a whole class, eliciting answers in full sentences using too/also/as well.
If you have extra time in the lesson, have pupils tell a partner what they did yesterday (i.e. what they would write in their diary about yesterday).
post: Choose an activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3 to review learning in this lesson or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book pp.14–17 for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 28 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 52 Picture or extract from a diary (and if possible a diary- style blog)
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider having pupils work in pairs of more and less proficient pupils for Step 5 to highlight all informal language in the diary entry. The more proficient pupil can support their peer at this point.

lessons.label: Writing 5
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Informal written language (e.g. Yuck!; Ha! Ha! Ha!)

pre: Choose an activity from the pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 to review the theme of Diaries refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book p.14–17 for more ideas.
delivery: Ask pupils to look again at the text on page 28 of the Pupil’s Book. Ask Whose diary is it? and Does Gemma use formal or informal language in her diary?

Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.52. Pupils analyse the language in the diary. Remind pupils that exclamation marks are used more often in informal writing than in more formal writing. Ask pupils to find more examples of punctuation in the diary. Note that brackets are often used in informal writing to add information like the example.

Follow the instructions for Activity 5 in the Teacher’s Book, p.52. Pupils put their ideas together to help plan for Activity 6. If they have no shared experience of a trip, have them think about a family trip they have been on. Have them make written notes together, which they can use to support writing in the next step of the lesson. Monitor and help pupils.

Follow the instructions for Activity 6 in the Teacher’s Book, p.52. Pupils write a diary entry about a school trip. Either they write together or they can support each other if their content is different.
post: Follow the instructions for Learning to Learn in the Teacher’s Book, p.52.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 28–29 Exercise(s): 4–6 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 52
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider brainstorming some informal vocabulary with pupils before they write (e.g. adjectives such as really horrible, awesome, fantastic, awful) to help pupils express themselves fully. Consider preparing a model diary for Activity 6 (step 5) to support pupils in writing.

lessons.label: Listening 5
lessons.focus: Past tenses review (including used to)

pre: Review the topic of life in the past using one of the activities from the pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book pp.14–17 for more ideas.
delivery: Have pupils look around the classroom. In groups, they write as many English words for things they can see in the classroom as possible on a large piece of paper. Give them two minutes for this.

Have pupils review the words they have brainstormed. They circle things which they think children could find in their classroom 50 (or 100) years ago. Gather some ideas from pupils. Write them on the board and focus on spelling at this stage.
Ask pupils to look at the picture of the classroom on page 27 of the Pupil’s Book. Ask them if they can see anything on their lists.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.50. Pupils listen for their words.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.51. Pupils review the main details of the text.

Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.51. Have pupils make notes about their ideas and conduct feedback on these and on any common language mistakes after pupils have finished this step.
Discuss the (CCE) Value question – see Teacher’s Book, p.51
post: Choose an activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3 to review learning in this lesson or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book pp.14–17 for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 27 Exercise(s): 1–4 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 50–51 Large sized paper for each group.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider reminding pupils that they do not need to focus on spelling at Step 2. At this stage, brainstorming is about giving ideas. If pupils don’t know a word they want to contribute in English, they can ask a friend or can put it in their home language and ask you later.

lessons.label: Speaking 5
lessons.focus: Future review (will and won’t; going to and present continuous)

pre: Play a game to review will and won’t, for example Stand up, Sit down: the teacher/a pupil says a sentence and pupils stand up if they agree or sit down if they disagree. Use statements which focus on schools and classrooms of the future. Remind pupils of the use of will and won’t to talk about predictions, and elicit from pupils how we talk about future plans (using going to or present continuous). This will give you an idea of pupils’ understanding of future forms for later in the year.
delivery: Show the pictures of futuristic classrooms. Talk to the pupils about what they show and ask for more ideas and opinions about how classrooms will be in the future. Make notes on the board.

Pupils work in groups of four. Set the main task (see Step 4). Have pupils discuss the task and decide on different roles within the group, for example one pupil to draw/design, one to write, one to search for or brainstorm ideas, one to prepare the presentation.

Pupils create a poster to show a classroom of the future. They will present their poster to the class in Step 5. Encourage pupils to label the poster. They should draft these labels before writing them on the poster. Encourage pupils to check spelling using a dictionary or to ask you. Pupils can use the internet to search for ideas if available, although monitor this to ensure safety online. Remind pupils to use as much English as they can when working in groups.
Groups present their poster to the class. Each group listening should ask at least one question or make one comment.
post: Give feedback on each group’s poster and presentation. Encourage peer feedback from the class on each one. Focus on content, language and teamwork as well as language.

lessons.materials: Pictures of futuristic classrooms Poster paper, pens and pencils for each group Dictionaries
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider encouraging more proficient pupils to add longer text to their poster, whereas less proficient pupils could simply write labels.

lessons.label: Language Arts 5
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friend
lessons.focus: Verbs (e.g. wiggle, kick, tickle, lick, count, run, walk)

pre: Pupils look at their toes and describe them e.g. tiny, small, round, long, big
Elicit from pupils why they like their toes and what their toes can do.
delivery: Pupils recite the poem.
Ask pupils to act out the verbs in the poem.
Pupils trace their feet on a card and cut it out.
Pupils write a thank you note to their feet on the card.
Pupils arrange their feet cards around the class. Pupils walk around the class following the feet cards and read what their friends have written on their cards.
post: Pupils share their personal experiences on how to take care of their feet.

lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider providing pupils with additional support/phrases they can use in their note.

lessons.label: Reading 6
lessons.focus: Past tenses review (e.g. Mr. Brockbank didn’t have a lamp. He had a candle.)

pre: Follow the instructions for the visualisation Warm-up: Time machine activity in the Teacher’s Book, p.56.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.56.
Have pupils write questions for their partner to check their ideas in Step 2 using really to check their understanding/ideas, for example What did Mr. Brockbank really switch on?
Pupils ask their partners the questions and discuss the answers.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.56. Focus again on spelling common words accurately.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.56. Pupils prepare a rewritten text in writing.
Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.57. Pupils share their ideas in groups. Monitor and note common mistakes at this step and Step 6.
post: Use your notes from monitoring for error correction as a whole class using the board or dictate sentences for pupils to correct.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 31 Exercise(s): 1–4 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 56–57
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider having very high proficiency pupils write more complex questions in Step 3, such as What do you think Mr. Brockbank switched on?, where the word order changes from simple question patterns.

lessons.label: Writing 6
lessons.focus: Past tenses review, e.g. He got up and checked the time on his mobile phone.

pre: Prepare a writing task to review the spelling of vocabulary from the unit.
delivery: Review pupils’ answers to Activity 3 on p.31 of the Pupil’s Book by asking questions about their text with a true-false activity.

In pairs or groups of three, have pupils brainstorm ideas for a very short extract or scene similar to that in Activity 1 on p.31 of the Pupil’s Book. The topic should be a scene from family life in their grandparents’ younger days. Encourage pupils to consider the past in their community. They should include three things from the wrong time. Have pupils use a dictionary to check spelling and meaning of words before asking you for help. This could be an online or paper-based dictionary.
Ask pupils to write a very short scene using the Activity 1 text as a model. They should include some direct speech in their scene.
Groups exchange their writing with another group. This group reads it to try to find and correct the three inaccuracies.

Give feedback on all aspects of each group’s work. Focus on the content of pupils’ work and discuss how life has changed positively since their grandparents’ were their age, making Malaysia a more modern society with easier living (CCE: Patriotism).
post: 6. Choose a post-lesson task from the activities in Section 3 to consolidate key language, or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book pp.14–17 for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 31 Exercise(s): 1–2 Worksheets: A spelling activity (Writing task) Dictionaries
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider supporting pupils at both the ideas stage and the drafting stage as they may find this writing task challenging. Try to have more proficient pupils working with less proficient ones, but take care that they all contribute equally.

lessons.label: Listening 6
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Future forms review, e.g. I think people will travel by plane.

pre: Ask the first Cooler question on p.51 of the Teacher’s Book. Have pupils discuss in small groups for five minutes and make notes. Gather feedback and take notes on the board.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Vocabulary in the Teacher’s Book, p.54.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.54. Pupils brainstorm more ideas about life in the future.

Write the words environment, technology and everyday family life on the board. Have some pupils come to the board and write words or phrases under each word relating to how these may be in the future.
Tell pupils you will give a short presentation about these topics. They should listen and decide which order you present the topics in. Give your presentation and give feedback on the answer.
Ask another gist question for each topic, for example asking if pupils agree with your ideas, or saying whether the predictions are positive or negative. Give your presentation again.
Pupils work in pairs. They ask and answer the question What are you going to do in the future? Their answers might relate to a job, or to some of your future predictions.
post: Choose a post-lesson task from the activities in Section 3 to review the main ideas from this lesson, or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17 for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 30 Exercise(s): 1 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 51, 54 Prepare a short presentation about three possible scenarios for life in the future (e.g. one about technology, one about environment, one about everyday family life)
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider providing some models of language and/or a review of future forms after Step 6 to support less proficient pupils.

lessons.label: Speaking 6
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Review of past and future forms; Functional language – checking understanding (e.g. Can I check something, please?)

pre: Choose a pre-lesson task from the activities in Section 3 to review the main ideas from recent lessons, or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17 for more ideas.
delivery: Have pupils look at the functional language in the Pupil’s Book, p.30 (phrases to check understanding of what a speaker is saying). Ask them to copy the phrases into their notebooks, leaving two lines between each one. 2. Have pupils look back on their work during this unit. Hand out the worksheet. As they review their work, have them fill in the table with ideas they have had and information they have found out in the unit so far relating to life in the past, life now and life in the future.

Divide the class into two halves. Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.54. Note that half of the pupils should follow the task as described, and the other half should role play as a museum guide in the year you are in now (e.g. 2021) looking back at the past. As they do the activity, they should try to use the functional language. When they use it, they can tick it in their notebooks. They should aim to use each phrase at least once.

Introduce the idea of ‘presentism’, which suggests that people find it difficult to think about the past or future without basing their ideas on the present. You may need to use a little of the pupils’ home language to explain this concept. Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.55. Pupils discuss what they think will seem strange to people in the future about our lives in the present. Pupils discuss in pairs or small groups. (CCE: Values).
Follow up with the question from the Cooler activity in the Teacher’s Book, p.55. This could be done as a whole class.
post: Choose a post-lesson task from the activities in Section 3 to review the main ideas from this lesson or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14-17 for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 30 Exercise(s): 2– 3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 54–55 Worksheet: A table with three columns, labelled past – present – future.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider giving pupils the choice of which time frame to work in for Step 3 (2021/this year or 2121/in 100 years from now). Use contribution cards to make sure all pupils participate in group discussions (e.g. each pupil has five tokens which they use when they say an idea. They should all use between three and five tokens).

lessons.label: Language Arts 6
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Verbs (simple present)

pre: Review the poem Toes.
Ask pupils to do the actions to revise the verbs.
delivery: Divide pupils into groups.
Give each group a body part. (e.g. eye, nose, hand)
Pupils discuss what functions/actions these parts can do. For example: eye: blink, wink, roll, see, stare hand: wave, shake, hold, touch, clap nose: blow, smell, twitch, breathe, sniff
Based on the original poem toes, pupils write their own poem by substituting the verbs that are suitable to the body parts assigned to their groups.
post: Pupils recite the poem to the class.
Pupils give feedback using Two Stars and a Wish: two things that are good (stars) and one thing that can be improved. (wish)

lessons.materials: Anthology of Poems for Year 4,5, and 6 Toes by Judith Nicholls Page: 30 Contemporary Children’s Literature Teaching Guidebook (BPK) – Poetry
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider getting less proficiency pupils to produce at least four lines and higher proficiency pupils to produce more than four lines in Step 6.

lessons.label: Language Awareness 2
lessons.focus: Teacher to complete:

std.note: Language Awareness lessons should be presented and practised using a Main Skill and a Complementary Skill (Listening, Speaking, Reading or Writing). Teachers can use the Content and Learning Standards in the Year 6 DSKP.

pre: Review language from Unit 2 with an activity from the list of pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14-17 for more ideas.
delivery: Choose from activities from the Review unit (Pupil’s Book, pp.32–33, Activities 1–5), which reviews the language, vocabulary and skills covered in Units 1 and 2. This choice should be based on your observations and notes on pupils’ progress and achievement in these units. Choose activities which will review areas pupils found challenging or which they may have forgotten. You could have pupils choose for themselves what they would like to do in the review unit. See Teacher’s Book, pp.58–59 for instructions for activities.

Set pupils a writing task which is based on the unit theme of past and future. Collect their work and give feedback on strengths and areas to work on. Note: ● Plan any further activities for this unit to develop language skills according to your pupils’ needs. ● You can use information about your pupils’ performance which you collected using formative assessment strategies while teaching this unit. ● The information could include your observation of pupils interacting in classroom activities and their performance in written activities. ● Plan activities which focus on language practice in a meaningful, fun and communicative way.
post: Ask pupils to think about their learning and performance in this unit. They then complete the self-assessment worksheet (see below and see note in Differentiation strategies column).
Collect the worksheets from pupils and review them to note pupils’ responses. If there are any areas of concern, prepare a review of these in upcoming lessons.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 32–33 Exercise(s): 1–5 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 58–59 Worksheet: A writing task. Self-assessment worksheet (see below)
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. Some pupils may need a little support understanding and completing the self- assessment worksheet, especially at the beginning of the year. Help pupils to express their ideas in English as you monitor.

lessons.label: Reading 7
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Past simple (e.g. I tried it this month.) & present perfect (e.g. I’ve never been kayaking before.)

pre: Follow the instructions for Warm-up: Can you guess? in the Teacher’s Book, p.60.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.60. Pupils are introduced to the text and use the pictures to predict content.
Ask pupils if they have ever done any of the activities in the pictures.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s book, p.61. Pupils read for global understanding to check their answers to Activity 1.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.61. Pupils guess the meaning of new words before checking them in the dictionary as necessary.

Ask pupils which country Emma is from (Canada). Elicit some ideas for similar activities people in Malaysia might do e.g. scuba diving, visiting tall buildings in Kuala Lumpur. Pupils could do this in pairs.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.62. Pupils read the blog posts again for specific information to answer the questions.

If you have time, follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.62. This could be an activity for fast finishers, or you could set this as homework if there is no time left in your main lesson.
post: Ask the follow-up questions in Activity 3 in the Pupil’s Book, p.36 for a whole class discussion.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 34–36 Exercise(s): 1–4, 1-3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 60–62
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider asking pupils to divide the words to guess in step 5 between them in a group. More proficient pupils could take more words than less proficient ones. Then pupils can share their findings with the group and peer-teach new words.

lessons.label: Writing 7
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Present perfect for experience + never (e.g. I’ve never seen a lion in the wild.)

pre: Follow instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.61 for Cooler: Physical spelling to review the vocabulary from the previous lesson.
delivery: Re-introduce Emma, the character from the blog in the Pupil’s Book pp.34–35. Ask pupils What exciting things has she done? Elicit some ideas. Where pupils don’t use the present perfect, reformulate their answers to the present perfect.

Using the worksheet, pupils read the sentences in the present perfect about Emma. In pairs, they decide if they are true or false. Note that the sentences should include examples of ‘has never’ as well as positive sentences.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.64. Pupils analyse the new language.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.64. Pupils complete a gap-fill activity to check their understanding.
Follow the instructions for Working with Words in the Teacher’s Book, p.63. Pupils focus on irregular verb forms again.
Ask pupils, individually, to write at least one more true sentence and at least one more false sentence about Emma in their notebooks.
Pupils exchange their sentences with a partner to read and decide if they are true or false.
Pupils correct all false sentences (Step 7 and Step 3).
post: Play a game of ‘Slap’ using the verb cards. Small groups spread out a set of verb cards. Say a sentence about Emma, about you or about pupils using the present perfect. Pupils listen and slap the main verb they hear. Extend to pupils giving sentences in their groups if you have time.

lessons.focus: Present perfect questions (e.g. Have you ever visited Tokyo? [Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.])

pre: Follow the instructions for Warm up: Camping experiences in the Teacher’s Book, p.66. Pupils brainstorm camping experiences. Ask pupils what they have done.
delivery: Follow instructions for Vocabulary in the Teacher’s Book, p.66. Pupils check their understanding of key words.
Follow instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.66. Pupils listen to and practise the dialogue.
Focus on the questions in the dialogue and ask pupils to underline them. Have pupils ask each other the questions. They give their own answers. Do not insist on full answers at this stage.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.66. Pupils prepare questions and then give their own answers. Have pupils prepare and answer one or two extra questions.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.67. Pupils ask each other the questions, including the extra one(s) they have prepared.
post: Follow the instructions in Extension in the Teacher’s Book, p.67. Pupils have further practice in forming and understanding questions. You could play between two large teams in your class, sitting face-to-face, depending on the size and layout of your class.

lessons.label: Speaking 7
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Present perfect statements (I’ve seen a lion.) and questions/answers: (Have you ever visited Tokyo?)

pre: Choose an activity from the pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 to review present perfect in questions and statements.
delivery: Have pupils sit in a circle. This could be on chairs or on the floor, depending on what is most suitable in your classroom. Show each picture card in turn. Elicit what the picture shows (e.g. swim in the sea/play a computer game, etc). Pass the card around the circle, pupils should say if they have/haven’t done this activity.

Still in the circle, have pupils ask another pupil in the circle Have you ever…?. The pupil answers and then asks another pupil the same question. Repeat several times with each card. You could then introduce several cards at once. Pupils will need to accompany speech with gestures, perhaps, if this becomes noisy.
Hand out the worksheet. Pupils complete the gapped Have you ever…? questions. Ask pupils to write between one and three extra Have you ever…? questions.

Pupils move around the classroom asking each other the questions. They should try to find someone who answers ‘yes’ to each question. They write the name of the person who says ‘yes’ next to the question.
Pupils return to their desks. They compare their findings with their partner by saying, for example, Adilah has been camping or Adam has been fishing.
post: Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.65 for Cooler: Experiences. Pupils review and consolidate the target language.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 37 Exercise(s): 3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 65 Worksheet: A ‘Find Someone Who’ survey with gapped Have you ever..? questions and space for a name next to the question. Allow space for extra questions. Picture cards using images from Pupil’s Book, p.37, Activity 3 (several copies for a large class).
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider extending pupils’ vocabulary in Step 2 with different pictures. If you have time, you could ask pupils to draw pictures of something interesting they have done. You could use their pictures instead of or as well as the pictures from the textbook.

lessons.focus: Past simple tense

pre: Pupils look at Akbar’s Dream book cover and identify the features of the book cover e.g. title, author, blurb, publisher
delivery: Pupils look at the cover and brainstorm ideas about what the story is about.
Divide pupils into small groups and distribute a set of pictures from the guidebook (page 36) to each group.
In groups, pupils discuss the pictures and create a possible story based on the pictures given.
Groups take turns to narrate their predicted story to their classmates. Other groups provide feedback on friends’ stories.
post: Pupils choose the story they think is most likely to happen. Teacher records the chosen predicted story and will revisit it once the pupils read and find out what happens.

lessons.label: Reading 8
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Past simple (e.g. I went skiing) & present perfect (e.g. the best I’ve ever done)

pre: Choose a pre-lesson task from the list in Section 3 which reviews present perfect forms or key vocabulary needed in this lesson relating to the text in the Pupil’s Book, pp.34–35.
delivery: Divide the class into three groups (A–C). Ask pupils to look at Emma’s blog entries for January (Pupil’s Book, p.34). They should highlight the information: Group A – What Emma did [I went skiing] Group B – Where Emma was [Whistler ski resort near Vancouver; Canada] Group C – Emma’s opinions [the views are amazing; it’s a really fun place with lots of exciting activities to try]

Draw a mind map on the board with three secondary bubbles. Ask a member of each group to come and write their answers around one bubble each. Elicit the headings for each bubble (What Emma did / Where Emma was / Emma’s opinions).
Guide pupils to understanding how mind maps work using the example on the board. Explain that these can help us brainstorm and organise ideas for writing, too.

Follow the instructions for Learning to Learn in the Teacher’s Book, p.70. Pupils look at another example of a mind map then create one from another of Emma’s blog entries. They will read for specific information to do this.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.70. Pupils analyse the features of blogs as a text type, having read for detail in the text.
post: Review any challenging vocabulary in the lesson with an activity from the tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17 for more ideas.

In addition, you may want to consider asking two pupils to come to the board from each group so that they can help each other complete the mind map on the board in step 3.

lessons.label: Writing 8
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Past simple (e.g. I went skiing) & present perfect (e.g. the best I’ve ever done)

pre: Choose a Pre-lesson task from the list in Section 3 to review vocabulary from the current topic.
delivery: Tell pupils it was your birthday at the weekend (or talk about your real birthday). Tell them what you did on your birthday.
Draw a mind map on the board with headings such as Where? What? Why? Opinion? etc. (relating to the content of your talk). Pupils copy the mind map into their notebooks.
Tell pupils again about your birthday. They listen and complete mind map with notes.
Pupils compare their mind maps in pairs before some come out to complete the mind map on the board.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.70. Pupils look at the pictures and complete the mind map.

Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.70. Pupils use the information on Pupil’s Book, p.41 to write. Pupils write on the writing task sheet (worksheet). Guide the task as necessary and support pupils (see Teacher’s Book, p.70) if they need it. Collect pupils’ writing for review. Give plenty of positive as well as constructive feedback to pupils to show them where to improve in relation to the assessment criteria for the writing assessment. Mark their papers using a correction code (i.e. highlight different kinds of mistakes without correcting them) for mistakes your pupils can correct themselves, especially in the use of past simple and present perfect, as well as punctuation, use of capitals and use of cohesive devices (linking words, e.g. but, because). Ignore more complex mistakes or give a correction. Pupils will work on a second draft in Lesson 44.
post: Choose a Cooler activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3 where pupils will be engaged in a fun, active game, or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14– 17 for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 41 Exercise(s): 2–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 70 Prepare a short talk about what you did on our birthday. Worksheet: A writing task sheet. The writing rubric should be based on the information in Activity 3, Pupil’s Book, p.41.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider nominating pupils who are more/less confident to come and write more complex/simpler answers on the mind map on the board in Step 5. See Teacher’s Book, p.70 for suggestions to support pupils. When reviewing pupils’ writing, in the case of low- proficiency pupils, focus on just a few mistakes and ignore others so as not to demotivate them.

lessons.focus: Present perfect review (e.g. What’s the worst experience you’ve ever had?)

pre: Introduce the topic of the listening text in the Pupil’s Book, p.39, with an activity from the pre-lesson tasks in Section 3.
delivery: Put up the pictures and ask pupils what they can see. Pre-teach and review some key vocabulary, but not the words in the box: say a word and ask pupils which picture it relates to. Explain or show pupils new vocabulary using the pictures.
Tell pupils they will listen to an interview. Check understanding of this word. Follow the steps for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.68.

Hand out the worksheet. Ask pupils to read the definitions. They could try to guess the words they are defining if possible. Play the recording again and ask pupils to try to hear a word which means the same as the definition.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book. Have pupils try to complete the fact files before listening again.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p. 69. Have pupils put in the answers from their memory first. Play the recording again only if necessary.
Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.69. Pupils talk about similarities and differences between Mike’s work and home life.
Follow the instructions for Cooler: All around the world in the Teacher’s Book, p.69. (CCE: Global Sustainability).
post: 8. Focus attention on the Values box on Pupil’s Book, p.39. Lead a class discussion about the benefits of travelling. (CCE: Values).

lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, in Step 4, you may want to consider putting individual definitions on slips of paper. Give some pupils two or three words to listen for and other pupils more, depending on their proficiency level.

lessons.label: Speaking 8
lessons.focus: Past tenses review

pre: Choose a pre-lesson task from the list in Section 3 which introduces or reviews the topic pupils will work with in this lesson.
delivery: Show the large copies of pictures in turn. For each, ask pupils to look at the picture and write three words about it in their notebooks. Put the pictures on the board.
Have pairs look at each other’s words. Conduct feedback and record useful words together on the board next to each picture. Drill any new words.

Tell pupils the pictures make two stories. Ask them to decide which pictures belong in each story, then in which order they think the pictures go in to make each story. Have pupils discuss in pairs possible story outlines. (CCE: Creativity & Innovation). Ask some pairs to tell the class their ideas.
Introduce the requirements of the speaking assessment, where pupils tell a short story using pictures. Tell pupils they will practise this in the lesson.

Pupils work in pairs. Hand out the worksheets, one A and one B for each pair. Pupils take turns to plan and tell their story based on the pictures on their version of the worksheet. They can use the vocabulary on the board to help, as they will have support in this way in the exam. Pupils should listen to each other and try to give some encouragement. They can also make notes about the story they hear.

Pupils exchange worksheets and re-tell their partner’s story. They should try to change at least three details of the story. Monitor as pupils do these tasks and note any common problem areas. You may want to identify individuals who will need extra support in developing skills for this task.
Ask pupils which story they prefer and why. This could be done as a whole class.
post: Give whole-class feedback on their performance on the task. Give plenty of positive feedback so that pupils feel confident as Speaking tests can be stressful or frightening for some children.

lessons.materials: Worksheets A & B: Two sets of pictures (one set for each Worksheet A and worksheet B) which tell a story (you could use those in the Workbook, p.32, Activity 2 and one other). Also, large copies of the pictures.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider having less proficient pupils listen to their partner telling each story first, and then try themselves.
